title: Seeds, Soil, and a Storm
overview: Jesus teaches through short stories about seeds and soil, explains why he speaks this way, and then calms a storm that leaves his followers wondering who he really is.

parts.label: The farmer and the seed (vv. 1-9)
parts.note: Farmers then scattered seed by hand across the whole field, so some landed on hard footpaths, thin soil over rock, or weedy patches. Much of it is lost, yet the good soil still yields a huge harvest, thirty to a hundred times what was sown.

parts.label: Why speak in stories (vv. 10-12)
parts.note: Jesus quotes Isaiah, where God warns the prophet that people will hear his message without taking it in. Scholars are unsure whether this means the stories are meant to hide truth from outsiders or simply that they expose who is truly listening.

parts.label: The story explained (vv. 13-20)
parts.note: The seed is God's message, and the four soils are four ways people respond: it is snatched away at once, it fades under hardship, it is crowded out by worry and money, or it takes root and bears fruit. Jesus seems surprised that even his closest followers needed this spelled out.

parts.label: Lamp and measure (vv. 21-25)
parts.note: A lamp is lit to give light, so what Jesus now says in veiled ways is meant to come into the open eventually. The saying about measuring likely means that those who listen closely will understand more, while careless listeners lose even what little they had.

parts.label: Two more seed stories (vv. 26-34)
parts.note: Planted seed grows on its own while the farmer sleeps, picturing God's kingdom, meaning God's rule, growing quietly toward a final harvest. The tiny mustard seed becoming a large shrub says it starts very small but ends up big enough to give shelter.

parts.label: Calming the storm (vv. 35-41)
parts.note: The Sea of Galilee is known for sudden violent winds, and even seasoned fishermen feared drowning while Jesus slept. In the Hebrew scriptures it is God who rules wind and sea, so Christians read the disciples' awed question about who Jesus is as pointing to him doing what God does.

disagreement: Christians differ on verses 11 and 12, whether Jesus used parables deliberately to keep some people from understanding or was describing how stories naturally reveal the hearts of those who refuse to listen.
think: When you hear something that seems to matter, what decides whether it stays with you or fades away?
